PullRequest.Title: Make hover mouseout dismissal tests deterministic
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #313831

## Summary
- Re-enable both skipped hover layout/dismissal regression tests (including the related re-entry coverage from #314025).
- Use text content with `hideOnHover: false` to preserve the same mouse tracking without creating a native `ResizeObserver`.
- Dispatch non-bubbling `mouseleave` events on the tracked hover container, and verify dismissal at the existing 200 ms debounce boundary with no intervening layouts.
- Keep production hover behavior unchanged.

## Root cause
The HTML fixture registered a native `ResizeObserver`, which is not controlled by the fake timer scheduler. Its initial callback could run after mouseleave but before the dismissal timer, triggering layout directly and again through the context view. Those layouts intentionally suppressed dismissal, violating the test's "no layout" premise. The original WebKit failure was reproduced locally, with a spy recording two unexpected layouts while the pointer was outside and the hover remained undisposed in the DOM. The historical change in #313832 only skipped the test.

## Validation
- Windows headless Chromium and WebKit, sequentially: the four `HoverService layout and resize` tests passed once per browser, followed by 25 additional fresh runs per browser. **208 passing test executions, zero failures or skips.**
- Test selection: `node test\unit\browser\index.js --browser chromium --browser webkit --sequential --run src\vs\platform\hover\test\browser\hoverService.test.ts --grep '^HoverService layout and resize'`.
- Focused transpilation, TypeScript dependency-graph check, ESLint, hygiene, and `git diff --check` passed. No broad build or dependency changes.
- macOS/Linux, Firefox, and Electron were not tested locally. Historical Actions logs returned HTTP 410 and their artifacts had expired.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hover mouseleave followed by a layout before the 200 ms dismissal debounce
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test creates one hover, dispatches one non-bubbling mouseleave, invokes one synchronous hover layout, and advances the virtual timer to 200 ms before asserting and explicitly disposing the hover. Production behavior is unchanged; only this browser-test path executes the new fixture and timing.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed cardinality: one hover, one mouseleave, one layout, and one timer callback per test execution.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One hover and one pending debounce timer are processed serially by VirtualTimeProcessor; there is no parallel work or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Cold and repeated runs perform the same fixed work; the string fixture avoids the prior native ResizeObserver callback.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed test and transitive HoverWidget/CompositeMouseTracker paths show the exact single layout, timer, listener, and disposal sequence.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact browser DOM/layout cost varies by runner, but the work is constant and fake-clock waiting does not add 200 ms of wall-clock latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff replaces an HTML fixture and native ResizeObserver with string content and one manual layout, reducing nondeterministic browser work without changing production paths.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hover mouseleave with no intervening layout
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The newly re-enabled test creates one hover, installs one Sinon method spy, dispatches one mouseleave, advances virtual time by 199 ms and then 1 ms, and lets the debounce dispose the hover before fixed-size assertions.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed cardinality: one hover, one listener event, one timer callback, one spy, and four scalar assertion fields per test execution.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single virtual timer runs serially; Sinon restoration occurs once in nested teardown.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or coalescing applies. Every run has identical bounded setup and cleanup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the test code, virtual scheduler cleanup, widget disposal, and suite teardown establish bounded resource lifetime.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact test-runner overhead of the Sinon spy is unmeasured, but it is one fixed spy and cannot scale with user data or lifetime.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Re-enabling one bounded fake-timer test adds negligible fixed CI work and does not affect the product runtime.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hover re-entry after a layout-suppressed mouseleave, followed by a second mouseleave
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The newly re-enabled test creates one hover, executes mouseleave/layout/virtual debounce, dispatches mouseover, then dispatches a second mouseleave and advances one more virtual debounce until disposal.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed cardinality: one hover, three synthetic mouse events, one explicit layout, and two bounded virtual-time advances.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most one debounce timer is active at each phase; mouseover clears the first timer state before the second leave, and all work is serialized by the virtual scheduler.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used. The string content path avoids ResizeObserver creation on both cold and repeated runs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: CompositeMouseTracker has one timer per tracker and HoverWidget disposal removes DOM/listeners; the changed test reaches this path once.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser layout duration is environment-dependent, but there is exactly one explicit layout and no collection-dependent fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The additional test exercises a constant amount of virtual-time and DOM work with bounded cleanup, while production code remains untouched.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete one-file, two-hunk inventory and traced the changed hover fixtures through HoverService, HoverWidget, CompositeMouseTracker, virtual timer scheduling, Sinon teardown, DOM/listener disposal, and observer creation. The PR only changes browser tests, removes native ResizeObserver use from these fixtures, and re-enables two fixed-cardinality tests. No actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
